P04|A.how: In form A members keep the template in step with the placements: they correct references against what is placed, replace stale plans and ask for warnings on obsolete templates so that repair does not undo the plan.

P14|A.how: In form A the lines restrict machine hands: scripts are offered, debated and refused, and the record shows the offer more than any placing by the room's own machines.

C01|A.how: In form A the lines restrict the claim that rooms worked without deciding their order: rooms divided the work, appointed representatives or assigned defenders, though implementation is not shown and the population count is not tested.

P23|A.how: In form A the chat needs upkeep: expired invitations are replaced, access is restored, and decisions are brought back to the thread for members outside the chat.

P14|B.how: In form B scripts are run as shared tools: targets and versions are kept in step so that friendly bots do not undo one another, and a script's fault is fixed without changing its target.

P23|B.how: In form B the chat works only on conditions: invitations that work and a current plan members can find; in r/reddevils a member approved the running script while refusing the chat, and the chat's own decisions stay unseen.

P02|C.how: In form C the design is settled for a time and reopened: a provisional choice made overnight, rough lettering to hold a gap, a finished mark followed by the next addition, and outside help turned into claims to label the mark.

P04|C.how: In form C the template is kept current: builders find mistaken blocks, retire outdated posts, announce changed locations and message the members who overwrite the design.

C01|C.how: In form C the lines restrict the claim that rooms worked without deciding their order: members divided outline and lettering, endorsed a template and assigned pixels or relay roles, without a formal office and without testing the count.

A11|C.how: In form C the template did not settle the design in most lines (40 of 58 fail as stated): colours, sizes and spacing stayed open, a redesign was repaired away as damage, or a dispute was settled by pointing to an image already in circulation.

P14|D.how: In form D the lines restrict machine hands: scripts were provided or offered and spare accounts were run by hand, without execution or extra placements shown.

A01|D.how: In form D the call and the building overlap: reports answer calls without showing that the call brought the builder, and an active builder also recruits.

A06|D.how: In form D scripts did not wait for upkeep under strain (12 of 21 lines fail as stated): they were offered for a new build or a move, spare accounts came during construction, and scripts kept plans accurate and covered absent members.

P02|E.how: In form E the design depends on the host and the means: a host's approval for space, the colours and size available, and the upkeep of a picture already standing.

P14|E.how: In form E machine hands help only on conditions: their targets must match the intended image and agreed overlaps, and a changed target must reach every runner.

P23|E.how: In form E the thread records chat invitations and claims brought back from the chat, not how the chat decided or whether planning moved there.

A01|E.how: In form E the call and the building appear apart in the record: replies do not show that the call brought the builders, and calls recur during building (E's account, section 8).

P03|F.how: In form F building returns after a move: a new spot or a replacement plan is followed by a new start and, in some rooms, a completed smaller mark.

P04|F.how: In form F the template moves with the spot: a new site gets an anchor coordinate, separate attempts converge on one build, and scarce hands make an exact first placement matter.

P14|F.how: In form F scripts and overlays are kept in step across accounts, and members switch automation off when they prefer to choose pixels by hand.

A06|F.how: In form F scripts came with the building, not after upkeep strained: a first request to coordinate construction, a script that promised to take space.
